study_identification_part.si4_title: Accommodating Site Variation In Neuroimaging Data Using Normative And Hierarchical Bayesian Models

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its objective to accommodate site effects in normative modeling using a hierarchical Bayesian approach and to compare it with other harmonization methods.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: In this study, we suggest accommodating for these site effects by including them as random effects in a hierarchical Bayesian model. We compared the performance of a linear and a non-linear hierarchical Bayesian model... to several harmonization techniques... In addition, we used data from individuals with autism to test whether our models are able to retain clinically useful information...

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study uses the ABIDE dataset. Eligibility criteria for the reference cohort (healthy controls) are described (573 age-matched typical controls). Image quality standards (outlier correction) are specified. Final sample size reported.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: For this study, we used 569 controls for development... out of which 470 were male... The data were processed using a standardized protocol... measures were scanned for outliers... removal of 1055 out of 162905 data points

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are used as covariates. Site effects are explicitly modeled using a hierarchical Bayesian model with site as a random effect.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: normative models with age and sex as covariates... In this study, we suggest accommodating for these site effects by including them as random effects in a hierarchical Bayesian model.
